items.bold: TRUMP NAMED GULF LEADERS who asked him to hold off attack: Qatar Emir Tamim, Saudi Crown Prince MBS, UAE President MBZ.
items.text: News9Live (1 day ago) confirmed: Trump elaborated on the strike cancellation, explicitly naming the Gulf Arab leaders who asked him to hold off: "I have been asked by the Emir of Qatar, Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, the Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia, Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud, and the President of the United Arab Emirates, Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, to hold off on our planned Military attack of the Islamic Republic of Iran, which was scheduled for tomorrow (Tuesday)." This reveals the Gulf Arab coalition against immediate US military action: Qatar (hosts Al Udeid Air Base), Saudi Arabia (OPEC swing producer), and UAE (Abraham Accords, Hormuz bypass) all simultaneously called Trump to delay the strike. This is the most important diplomatic revelation: even the US's closest Gulf allies do not want a full US military strike on Iran. They want a negotiated solution — and they used their direct access to Trump to delay the attack while negotiations continue.

items.bold: IRAN (Tasnim): "Will NEVER ACCEPT ending war in exchange for nuclear commitments." Diplomacy "continuous process."
items.text: CBS News live (20 hours ago) confirmed: "The Americans must understand that Iran will never accept ending the war in exchange for nuclear commitments," Tasnim (IRGC-linked news agency) quoted a source as saying, while reiterating Iran's longtime stance that the regime has no intention of building a nuclear weapon. Iran's government separately said Monday that indirect diplomacy with the US, brokered by Pakistani intermediaries, was "a continuous process" and that it had conveyed its latest positions to Washington. The two statements together define Iran's position: willing to negotiate a war-end deal, but nuclear is off the table entirely. Trump admin's top issue is nuclear. Iran's bottom line is nuclear non-negotiable. The gap that has persisted across 82 days remains the same. Gulf leaders buying time — not closing the gap.

items.bold: UAE BARAKAH NUCLEAR PLANT: IAEA confirmed reactor switched to EMERGENCY DIESEL GENERATORS after drone. No radiation leak.
items.text: DSIJ Insights (2 days ago) confirmed: a drone strike near the Barakah Nuclear Energy Plant in the UAE triggered fresh geopolitical concerns. The UAE Defence Ministry confirmed that two drones were intercepted, while another drone struck near the facility. The International Atomic Energy Agency stated that one reactor briefly switched to emergency diesel generators following the incident. No radiation leak or casualties were reported. This is the first confirmed incident where a nuclear power reactor (not just a weapons facility) switched to emergency backup power as a result of a drone attack during the 82-day war. Barakah is the UAE's civilian nuclear power plant — its targeting by Iran is a fundamental escalation threshold. The IAEA response (confirming the generator switch) makes this a formally documented nuclear infrastructure incident of the war.

military.t: UAE BARAKAH NUCLEAR PLANT: IAEA Confirmed Reactor Switched to Emergency Diesel Generators. One Drone Struck Near Facility.
military.d: DSIJ Insights (2 days ago) and CBS News confirmed: the International Atomic Energy Agency stated that one reactor at the UAE's Barakah Nuclear Energy Plant briefly switched to emergency diesel generators following the drone attack. Barakah is a 4-unit Korean-designed APR-1400 reactor complex — the Arab world's first nuclear power plant. Its targeting by Iran crosses a new threshold. The IAEA has now documented nuclear safety concerns at two sites: Bushehr (weapons program, IAEA warned early in war) and Barakah (civilian power, UAE).

assessment.body:
Wednesday 7:30 AM IST. Day 82. The diplomatic picture clarifies — and the gap remains.

THE GULF LEADERS REVELATION
Trump named them: Qatar's Emir Tamim, Saudi Crown Prince MBS, UAE President MBZ.
All three called Trump to delay the Tuesday strike simultaneously.
What this means:
• Qatar: hosts Al Udeid Air Base (10,000 US troops, CENTCOM HQ) — most important US military hub in the Middle East. Qatar asked Trump not to strike.
• Saudi Arabia: OPEC swing producer, Petroline bypass route. MBS asked Trump to wait.
• UAE: Abraham Accords partner, Hormuz coastal state, Barakah nuclear plant just struck. MBZ asked Trump to hold.
Verdict: Even after Iran attacked UAE's nuclear power plant, MBZ asked Trump not to strike Iran.
The Gulf Arab preference: negotiated solution, not military escalation.

IRAN's BOTTOM LINE
"Will NEVER accept ending the war in exchange for nuclear commitments."
Diplomacy is a "continuous process" — but nuclear is off the table.
Trump's top issue = nuclear. Iran's bottom line = never nuclear.
Gulf leaders can delay the strike. They cannot close the nuclear gap.

THE BARAKAH IAEA INCIDENT
One reactor switched to emergency diesel generators.
Two drones intercepted, one struck near the plant.
No radiation. No casualties. But IAEA has now documented it.
Iran attacked the UAE's civilian nuclear power plant — and the UAE still asked Trump not to strike Iran.
This tells you everything about Gulf Arab risk calculation.

INDIA's WEDNESDAY
• IOC Q4 results today — first major OMC earnings under war pressure
• Gulf leaders named: engage Qatar, Saudi, UAE bilaterally
• Iran nuclear gap = no deal imminent; act independently
• Kharif fertiliser: 55 vessels/week = order today
• Bessent license: engage Treasury
• Haji Ali MEA protest: overdue

ING's WARNING
"Re-escalation risks are increasing."
"China pressure on Iran possibly misplaced."
Gold at $4,600 — markets pricing uncertainty, not resolution.
Brent ~$109 — elevated but off $112 peak.

VERDICT: Day 82 opens with the clearest picture yet of why this war is stuck. Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE — all US allies who have been attacked by Iran — are asking Trump not to strike. Iran is saying it will never discuss nuclear. ING is saying re-escalation risks are increasing. And India has IOC Q4 results to digest, kharif fertiliser orders to place, and a formal Haji Ali protest to file. The gap between the two sides is nuclear-sized. The Gulf Arabs are buying days, not closing it.
